# Nikita Rabykin

> Full-stack developer based in Helsinki, Finland, with eleven years of production experience across backend, frontend and cloud infrastructure. Currently the sole architect and lead developer of the entire technical stack of a Finnish tour operator (Aikamatkat Oy / Timetravels), from Terraform and Kubernetes up to the storefront and internal tools.

This file is the machine-readable version of the CV at https://rabykin.dev. It is intended for AI agents, LLM crawlers and recruiting tools. All content here is public and may be indexed, quoted and summarised. The HTML page at https://rabykin.dev is the canonical human-readable version and is print-ready (A4).

## Availability and preferred engagements

- Open to: consulting and contracting engagements first; also software architect and senior developer positions. Formats: project-based delivery, fractional architect or technical lead, senior developer embedded in a team. Remote, or on site in Helsinki, Finland.
- Scope of a typical engagement: gathering business requirements from stakeholders, identifying the actual problem behind the request, proposing and designing the solution, validating it, implementing it, releasing it to production, handing it over to or integrating it with the client's team, and supporting it afterwards.
- Working style: understands the problem and proposes a design before writing code, rather than executing tickets against a finished specification. Best fit for clients who need one person to think, decide and deliver.
- Covers every layer alone when needed: cloud infrastructure (AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, GitOps), backend (PHP/Magento 2, Laravel, Node.js), frontend (React, TypeScript), data and analytics (ClickHouse, Airbyte, Metabase), payment and third-party integrations, observability. Reference case: the Timetravels platform in the Experience section, a €10M-revenue e-commerce and booking operation built and run single-handedly.
- Leadership: has led teams of up to four developers, mentored juniors, and owned code and architecture review as project lead. Available for technical leadership, audits and architecture reviews of existing systems.
- Domains with the deepest track record: e-commerce and booking platforms, Magento 2 at scale, Laravel applications, headless storefronts, cloud migration and Kubernetes adoption, self-hosted data and internal tooling replacing paid SaaS, payment integrations (Stripe, banks).
- Contact: nikita.rabykin@gmail.com.

## Approach to tooling: research first, build only where nothing fits

- Default is to adopt an existing product. Custom code is reserved for the parts that are genuinely specific to the business, such as the tour booking model inside Magento 2. The self-hosted toolchain at Timetravels (ArgoCD, External Secrets, Airbyte, ClickHouse, Metabase, n8n, Outline, New Relic and others) is entirely off-the-shelf software, selected and operated rather than written.
- Whatever is used for a test or an MVP tends to end up in production, so evaluation happens before adoption, not after. Kubernetes and Helm make this cheap: candidate products are deployed in isolation, tried against real data, and kept or discarded. Dozens have been trialled this way; around twenty stayed.
- Case, business intelligence: dashboard requests kept arriving and each one hand-built in the store was a heavy task. Instead of building the next one, a week went into comparing Apache Superset, Metabase, Grafana, Redash and several other tools on the actual data. Metabase won. Dashboard turnaround dropped from days to minutes, reports that used to be copied into spreadsheets and shared with outside people now sit behind one login with managed access, and staff can now query any data themselves in natural language through an AI layer on top of it.
- Case, email marketing: the team was leaning towards Mailchimp. A comparison of a dozen services showed that most charge per contact, which fits badly with a contact base that grows quickly every year and a channel whose value was still unproven. Pay-per-send pricing made more sense, so a small self-hosted sender on top of Mailjet was chosen instead, at a small fraction of the subscription cost.
- The open-source projects on GitHub (macOS utilities, a Wolt CLI, a tip jar app) are personal tools built for the fun of it. At work the bar for writing something new is that the market has been checked first and nothing fits the requirement or the cost model.

## Experience

### Aikamatkat Oy (Timetravels) — Architect & Lead Developer
- Period: February 2023 – present
- Location: Helsinki, Finland
- Company: Finnish tour operator; online sales of guided tours to Lapland and Nordic destinations
- Responsibilities and achievements:
  - Designed and operates an AWS EKS cluster provisioned with Terraform: VPC, IRSA, autoscaling node groups, EBS/EFS CSI drivers, AWS Load Balancer Controller, External Secrets. All workloads delivered through ArgoCD GitOps with Argo Rollouts.
  - Authors in-house Helm charts for Magento 2, WordPress and internal services. Self-hosts the company's internal toolchain instead of paid SaaS: ClickHouse and Metabase (analytics), Airbyte (data ingestion), n8n (workflow automation), Outline (wiki), around 20 applications in total.
  - Built the analytics platform: a warehouse consolidating the whole business. Airbyte pipelines from Google Analytics, Google Search Console, Meta Ads, Stripe and Bókun, plus MySQL-to-ClickHouse CDC replication of the store database. Reported through Metabase dashboards used daily by sales, operations and finance.
  - Turned Magento 2 into a genuine tour booking system through roughly 180 in-house modules: a tour product model (departures, itineraries, accommodation, activities, pickup points, price categories) with its own admin UI, date-based availability with waiting lists, and passenger lists with group-leader management.
  - Built the commerce edges: Stripe and OP Bank payment flows with online refunds and back-office payments, template-driven bulk generation of a full season's products, order automation, and the GraphQL layer consumed by the storefront.
  - Rebuilt the storefront as a headless React server-side-rendered frontend on the Magento 2 GraphQL API (TypeScript, Vite, Node.js/Express).
  - Self-hosting the platform keeps total running cost to a fraction of the €100–150k per year that commercial managed alternatives would charge.
  - Carries the platform through season openings, when most of a year's bookings arrive within a few days: autoscaling on EKS, blue-green releases that never pause sales, New Relic APM across backend traces, logs and browser-side performance.
  - Built List Builder, the internal operations tool (Laravel, React, Inertia.js, TypeScript) that replaced the spreadsheet workflow for assigning travellers to buses, ferries and hotels.
- Technologies: AWS (EKS, RDS, EFS, ECR), Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, ArgoCD, Argo Rollouts, Docker, GitHub Actions, New Relic, Cloudflare, Magento 2, PHP, GraphQL, MySQL, ClickHouse, Airbyte, Metabase, n8n, Laravel, React, Inertia.js, TypeScript, Vite, Node.js, Express, Stripe, OP Bank

## Open Source

- live.tips (https://live.tips): live tip jar for street performers. One QR code on stage, tips paid directly into the artist's own Stripe account and shown live on their device. Flutter, Firebase.
- ClipSlop (https://github.com/mekedron/ClipSlop): system-wide AI text transformations for macOS bound to hotkeys, across OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama and any compatible provider. Swift, SwiftUI.
- wolt-cli (https://github.com/mekedron/wolt-cli) and wolt-stats (https://github.com/mekedron/wolt-stats): unofficial Go CLI for Wolt (browse venues, search items, build a cart from the terminal) paired with a dashboard that syncs order history into local SQLite. Go, SvelteKit.
- PieSwitcher (https://github.com/mekedron/PieSwitcher): radial window switcher for macOS, a pie-menu replacement for Cmd-Tab and Mission Control. Swift, SwiftUI.
- HiddenBarIcons (https://github.com/mekedron/HiddenBarIcons): menu-bar utility that recovers the icons macOS hides under the MacBook notch. Shipped via Homebrew with Sparkle auto-updates. Swift.
